title: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab versus sorafenib for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma
journal: New England Journal of Medicine; updated analysis in Journal of Hepatology
population: 501 systemic-treatment-naive patients with unresectable HCC, predominantly Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0–1
treatment: Atezolizumab 1,200 mg IV plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks versus sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily
summary: At updated median follow-up of 15.6 months, median OS was 19.2 vs 13.4 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.52–0.85). At 18 months, OS was 52% vs 40%, an absolute improvement of 12 percentage points (NNT ≈9 at 18 months). Median PFS was 6.9 vs 4.3 months (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.53–0.81).
criticalReview: This is a clinically important first-line advance over sorafenib for appropriately selected unresectable HCC. Grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events were 43% vs 46%, and grade 5 events 2% vs <1% in the updated analysis; do not calculate NNH from these non-increased aggregate toxicity rates. Bevacizumab-associated bleeding risk is central: assess portal hypertension and varices, and manage varices before treatment. Evidence chiefly applies to Child-Pugh A, ECOG 0–1 patients; do not extrapolate automatically to decompensated cirrhosis or compare directly with other modern first-line combinations.

absoluteEffect.toxicity: Grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs 43% vs 46%; grade 5 2% vs <1%
absoluteEffect.nnh: Not quantifiable as an excess harm endpoint
